reading.body:
James Justice's AI record is two cosponsorships and twelve recorded votes, all on one bill, S. 2296, across September and October 2025.

The two cosponsorships are the only affirmative legislative acts in the data. He cosponsored S. 3586, the AI for Mainstreet Act, in January 2026, and S. 5117, the Senior Chatbot Protection Act, in July 2026. Both dates are the bills' latest status dates, not the dates he signed on, so the record shows where the bills stood, not when he joined them.

The twelve votes are concentrated on S. 2296. He voted Yea on cloture, on the motion to proceed, on the motion to table an amendment, and on passage. He split on the amendments themselves, with two Yea and six Nay. The data records the votes but not what any amendment would have done, so the split cannot be read as a position on AI policy specifically.

Nothing here connects to compute, buildings, or power. The summary says the page also holds money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, but no such event appears in the fourteen points. The record covers one senator's floor activity on AI-related legislation and nothing about data centers, electricity, or the infrastructure that constrains AI scaling.
